Desire of All Nations
dee-ZYRE of all NAY-shunz
noun
Hebrew Chemdat Goyim (H2532 + H1471) — "Desire of nations"; Messianic title in Haggai 2:7, where God promises that the desire of all nations would come to fill the second temple with glory greater than the first.

Biblical Definition

Desire of All Nations is the Messianic title in Haggai 2:6-9 — God's promise during the construction of the second temple (Zerubbabel's temple, rebuilt after the Babylonian exile, completed 516 BC) that this rebuilt temple, though smaller and less ornate than Solomon's, would be filled with greater glory than the original: "For thus saith the LORD of hosts; Yet once, it is a little while, and I will shake the heavens, and the earth, and the sea, and the dry land; And I will shake all nations, and the DESIRE OF ALL NATIONS shall come: and I will fill this house with glory, saith the LORD of hosts. The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the LORD of hosts. The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former, saith the LORD of hosts: and in this place will I give peace." The promise was fulfilled when Christ — the desire-and-fulfillment of every true longing of every nation — physically walked into the second temple as a young child (presentation, Luke 2:22-39), as a boy (in his Father's house, Luke 2:46-49), and as the Messianic teacher cleansing and teaching there throughout His ministry. The second temple's glory was not silver and gold; it was the presence of God Himself in flesh walking its courts. The title preaches that whatever every nation truly longs for — peace, righteousness, justice, glory — is found in the Person of Christ. Behind every false god, every cultural deity, every pagan striving, lies the hidden Desire of All Nations. The gospel's missionary thrust is the announcement: the One whom every culture has unknowingly longed for has come.

Webster 1828 Definition

Messianic title in Haggai 2:7; Christ as the one who would come to the second temple and give it glory greater than the first; the universal longing of every nation embodied.

DESIRE OF ALL NATIONS, noun. Messianic title in Haggai 2:7. Hebrew Chemdat Goyim.

Promised during the construction of the second temple (516 BC); the glory of the second temple would exceed the first because the Desire of All Nations would come to it — fulfilled in Christ's physical presence in the temple courts.

Key Scripture

Haggai 2:7-9 — "And I will shake all nations, and the desire of all nations shall come: and I will fill this house with glory, saith the LORD of hosts. The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the LORD of hosts. The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former, saith the LORD of hosts: and in this place will I give peace."

Luke 2:27-32 — "And he came by the Spirit into the temple: and when the parents brought in the child Jesus... Then took he him up in his arms, and blessed God, and said, Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word: For mine eyes have seen thy salvation."

John 2:13-16 — "And the Jews' passover was at hand, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem, And found in the temple those that sold oxen and sheep and doves... And said unto them that sold doves, Take these things hence; make not my Father's house an house of merchandise."

Romans 1:14 — "I am debtor both to the Greeks, and to the Barbarians; both to the wise, and to the unwise."

Modern Corruption

Desire of All Nations is corrupted when the second-temple fulfillment context is lost (treating Haggai 2:7 as generic Messianic hope unrelated to Christ's specific temple-walking ministry), or when interfaith universalism flattens the title to "every religion's quest is valid."

expand to see more

Second-temple-fulfillment severance. Haggai's specific promise was that THIS second temple — being built before Haggai's eyes — would have greater glory than Solomon's first temple. The fulfillment came when Christ physically walked through this very temple (the second temple stood from 516 BC to AD 70). The Desire of All Nations CAME PHYSICALLY to the temple — that is the prophecy fulfilled. To read Haggai's promise as merely vague Messianic hope unrelated to Christ's temple ministry is to miss the canonical fulfillment.

Interfaith-quest universalism. Some interfaith dialogue takes "Desire of All Nations" to mean: every nation's religious quest is legitimate and points to the same truth. But the canonical title is sharper: the LONGING of every nation is real, but the FULFILLMENT is only in Christ. Every pagan god is the misdirected echo of a true longing for God; every cultural striving is the misshapen reach for what Christ alone supplies. The Desire of All Nations is not validation of every religion; it is the announcement that the true Object of every longing has come, and every counterfeit must yield to Him.

Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Chemdat Goyim (H2532 + H1471) — Desire of Nations; Messianic title in Haggai 2:7; Christ as the universal longing fulfilled in the second temple.

expand to see more

Hebrew chemdah (H2532) — desire, delight; goyim (H1471) — nations, Gentiles

Appears at Haggai 2:7 — during construction of the second temple (516 BC) — God promises the Desire of Nations will come

Fulfilled in Christ's physical presence in the temple: presentation (Luke 2), boyhood (Luke 2:46-49), ministry (John 2; Mark 11; etc.)

Universal longing: every nation's true religious quest finds its object in Christ; every false god is the misdirected echo

Usage

"The Desire of All Nations shall come — God's promise during the second temple's construction, fulfilled when Christ walked its courts."

"Behind every culture's false god lies the hidden Desire of All Nations; the gospel announces that the true Object has come."

"The glory of the second temple exceeded the first not in gold but in the presence of God Himself in flesh."
